QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_6

question.text: A prospective LP, Mr. Aditya Bhattacharya, asks you to explain how your Category III AIF structurally differs from a Mutual Fund. Which of the following is NOT a correct point of distinction?

answer.text: AIF corpus must be at least INR 20 crore; Mutual Funds have no minimum corpus requirement
AIF permits leverage and long-short strategies; Mutual Funds generally do not permit leverage
AIF is issued via private placement to a maximum of 1,000 investors; Mutual Funds are issued via public issue with no investor cap
The AIF Manager must contribute 1% of scheme corpus or INR 50 lakh whichever is lower, identical to the Mutual Fund sponsor contribution requirement

explanation.text: The Logic: Option D is the FALSE statement. As per Table 6.4, the MUTUAL FUND sponsor must contribute 1% of scheme amount or INR 50 lakh whichever is LOWER. The AIF Manager/Sponsor commitment is 5% of corpus or INR 10 crore whichever is LOWER (for Cat I/II, 2.5% or INR 5 crore). Options A, B and C are all accurate distinctions from Table 6.4. The Trap: Option D is designed to trap candidates who conflate the two skin-in-the-game regimes. The 1%/INR 50 lakh MF number and the 5%/INR 10 crore AIF number are both in the same table and easily confused. Cross-Exam Context: NISM Series V-A (MF Distributor) tests the MF sponsor contribution; XIX-C tests the AIF side. The Manager exam specifically demands you know BOTH to answer LP due-diligence queries. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching a Cat III fund to an LP coming from the MF world, proactively explain skin-in-the-game — the 5%/INR 10 crore AIF commitment is materially larger than the MF 1%/INR 50 lakh standard and is a genuine differentiator to highlight, not hide.
